rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence yet about which modality, encoder, profile setting, or fusion strategy is most useful. The main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a competitive baseline and what performance level should be expected before adding complexity. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-based configuration without image, aggregation, or fusion confounds. It is the best next experiment because it establishes a clean reference point for later comparisons of RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion while avoiding premature investment in more complex designs.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only single-profile baseline using PCA, so it is still unclear whether the image modality provides useful signal at all. Testing image-only single-profile ResNet50 establishes a comparable unimodal baseline and isolates the effect of modality before investing in more complex multiprofile or multimodal fusion settings. This is the best next experiment because it reduces major uncertainty about which modality is more informative under a limited budget.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet50 (0.485 vs 0.208 accuracy), so RNA is the more promising modality, but it is unclear whether multiple profiles add useful information. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and modality as config_001 and changes only to multiprofile with avgpool, isolating the effect of profile aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, informative extension of the current best baseline, directly tests whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the strongest modality, and will guide whether to invest further in multiprofile RNA or multimodal configurations.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002, accuracy 0.5907), clearly better than single-profile PCA (config_001, 0.4849) and much better than image-only ResNet50 (config_010, 0.2079). This suggests multiprofile RNA representation is promising, but it is still unclear whether transformer aggregation would improve on avgpool. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA setup, so it isolates the effect of aggregation in the currently best direction. Under a limited budget, this is the most informative next step before adding image modality or fusion, because it tests an important design choice with minimal confounding changes.

RNA multiprofile with avgpool is currently the strongest direction (acc 0.591, F1 0.573), while image-only ResNet singleprofile is weak (acc 0.208). The key uncertainty is whether image features can benefit from the same multiprofile/avgpool setting that helped RNA, or whether image is simply uninformative. config_011 changes only profile/aggregation from config_010, isolating that effect for the image modality. It is a minimal, high-information experiment before investing in multimodal fusion or stronger image encoders, and it avoids changing model setting and fusion prematurely.

Multiprofile avgpool is the strongest known setting for both PCA RNA (0.591 acc / 0.573 F1) and ResNet50 image (0.328 acc), while transformer aggregation is worse for RNA. The key uncertainty is whether fusing these validated unimodal representations adds value over the RNA-only baseline. config_018 tests simple concat fusion of PCA RNA and ResNet50 image under the same multiprofile avgpool settings, isolating the fusion/multimodal effect without introducing untested encoders. This is the best next use of budget because it directly tests the central multimodal question, exploits the strongest profile/aggregation evidence, and will guide whether to invest in weighted fusion, ViT, or alternative RNA encoders.

The strongest completed result is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) with validation accuracy 0.6186 and F1 0.6103, showing that combining RNA and image features with avgpool aggregation is promising. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the fusion strategy matters: concat may be sufficient, or weighted fusion may better balance the modalities. config_019 tests exactly that by changing only fusion from concat to weighted while keeping the best-known profile, aggregation, encoders, and model setting fixed. This is the most efficient next experiment because it exploits the current best direction, isolates one important design decision, and will guide whether future effort should focus on fusion tuning or stronger representations such as ViT or transformer aggregation.

The strongest evidence so far is that multimodal multiprofile PCA + ResNet with avgpool and weighted fusion is the best configuration (0.639 accuracy, 0.620 F1), improving over RNA-only PCA avgpool and weak image-only ResNet models. A major remaining uncertainty is whether the image branch is limited by the ResNet encoder, since only ResNet has been tested for images. config_025 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the proven multiprofile, avgpool, weighted-fusion, PCA-RNA setup. This cleanly tests whether a stronger image representation can improve the current best architecture and clarify whether image encoding is a key bottleneck. It is a high-value one-factor extension: it may yield immediate gains and, either way, tells us whether to invest further in image encoders or shift focus to RNA encoders and aggregation.

The strongest evidence so far is for multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, with config_019 achieving the best validation accuracy (0.639) and F1 (0.620). The major untested design choice in this promising region is RNA representation, since only PCA has been evaluated. config_031 keeps the current best profile setting, image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed while replacing PCA with scvi_n200, directly testing whether a learned RNA encoder improves the current best multimodal setup. This is a one-factor extension of the most promising direction, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of an important untested representation choice, and it can either produce a new best result or efficiently rule out scvi before spending more experiments on related variants.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA is more informative than image alone, multiprofile with avgpool and weighted fusion improves multimodal performance, and scvi clearly outperforms PCA in the same multimodal resnet avgpool weighted setting (0.6776 acc / 0.6464 F1 vs 0.6390 acc / 0.6197 F1). The key remaining uncertainty is whether scgpt is a better RNA representation than scvi. config_043 changes only the RNA encoder from scvi to scgpt while preserving the best-supported multimodal multiprofile resnet avgpool weighted scaffold, directly testing representation quality and potentially identifying a higher-performing configuration.
